practical_skills: Reading a card statement line by line

sections.skill: Read a credit card statement and decide how much to pay and when

questions.prompt:
Credit card statement (closing date May 20): Previous balance $640.00 | Payments −$640.00 | Purchases +$412.75 | Fees $0.00 | Interest charged $0.00 | New balance $412.75 | Minimum payment due $25.00 | Payment due date June 15 | Purchase APR 22.99%
How much must Rosa pay by June 15 to avoid ANY interest on these purchases?
questions.intro: A credit card statement lists the previous balance, payments, new purchases, fees, interest, the new (statement) balance, the minimum payment, and the due date. Paying the full statement balance by the due date avoids interest on purchases (the grace period).
questions.feedback: Paying the full new balance, $412.75, by June 15 keeps the grace period.
sources: CFPB (Credit CARD Act / Regulation Z): Card issuers must mail statements at least 21 days before the due date; statements show the minimum payment warning; applicants under 21 need independent income or a cosigner. (https://www.consumerfinance.gov/consumer-tools/credit-cards/answers/key-terms/)

questions.prompt:
Credit card statement (closing date May 20): Previous balance $640.00 | Payments −$640.00 | Purchases +$412.75 | Fees $0.00 | Interest charged $0.00 | New balance $412.75 | Minimum payment due $25.00 | Payment due date June 15 | Purchase APR 22.99%
What is the LEAST Rosa can pay by June 15 and keep her account in good standing?
questions.intro: The minimum payment due is the smallest amount that avoids a late fee that month. Paying only the minimum leaves the rest of the balance owed, and interest is charged on it.
questions.feedback: The minimum payment due is $25.00; paying only that leaves $387.75 to carry over with interest.
sources: CFPB (Credit CARD Act / Regulation Z): Card issuers must mail statements at least 21 days before the due date; statements show the minimum payment warning; applicants under 21 need independent income or a cosigner. (https://www.consumerfinance.gov/consumer-tools/credit-cards/answers/key-terms/)

questions.prompt:
Credit card statement (closing date May 20): Previous balance $640.00 | Payments −$640.00 | Purchases +$412.75 | Fees $0.00 | Interest charged $0.00 | New balance $412.75 | Minimum payment due $25.00 | Payment due date June 15 | Purchase APR 22.99%
If Rosa pays only the $25 minimum, what balance carries into next month before interest?
questions.feedback: $412.75 − $25.00 = $387.75, which will then be charged interest.

questions.prompt:
Credit card statement (closing date May 20): Previous balance $640.00 | Payments −$640.00 | Purchases +$412.75 | Fees $0.00 | Interest charged $0.00 | New balance $412.75 | Minimum payment due $25.00 | Payment due date June 15 | Purchase APR 22.99%
The statement shows "Interest charged $0.00." Why?

choices.text: Paying the last balance in full kept the grace period
Her card has no interest rate at all
Interest is only charged in June
The card issuer forgot to add this month's interest charge

questions.correct_answer: Paying the last balance in full kept the grace period
questions.intro: When the previous statement balance was paid in full by its due date, new purchases usually get a grace period, so no purchase interest appears on the next statement.
questions.feedback: Paying the full $640 previous balance kept the grace period.

(https://www.consumerfinance.gov/consumer-tools/credit-cards/answers/key-terms/)

questions.prompt: A statement's "minimum payment warning" says paying only the minimum will take 9 years and cost $2,100 in total on a $1,000 balance. What does this tell the cardholder?

choices.text: The minimum payment is always the best choice
The remaining balance will be forgiven after 9 years
The minimum route costs far more and takes longer
The interest rate will drop to 0%

questions.correct_answer: The minimum route costs far more and takes longer
questions.intro: Federal law requires statements to show how long it would take to pay off the balance making only minimum payments, and the total cost, compared with a payment that pays it off in 3 years.
questions.feedback: $2,100 total for a $1,000 balance means $1,100 in interest.

sections.skill: Due dates, balances, and payments on a bill
sections.relationship: Reading a statement requires telling apart the balance, the minimum, and the due date.

questions.prompt: On a bill, what is the "due date"?

choices.text: The deadline to make a payment
The date the purchase was made
The date the card expires
The day interest is waived forever

questions.correct_answer: The deadline to make a payment
questions.intro: The due date is the deadline for the payment. Paying after it can bring late fees and other consequences.
questions.feedback: The due date is the payment deadline.
sources: CFPB (Credit CARD Act / Regulation Z): Card issuers must mail statements at least 21 days before the due date; statements show the minimum payment warning; applicants under 21 need independent income or a cosigner. questions.prompt: A bill shows a balance of $300 and a minimum payment of $25. Which payment pays it off?
questions.intro: The balance is the total owed. Paying the full balance clears the debt.
sources: CFPB (Credit CARD Act / Regulation Z): Card issuers must mail statements at least 21 days before the due date; statements show the minimum payment warning; applicants under 21 need independent income or a cosigner. questions.prompt: Which number on a statement is the total amount owed at closing?

choices.text: The minimum payment due this month
The credit limit
The new (statement) balance
The APR

questions.intro: The new balance (statement balance) is everything owed as of the closing date.
questions.feedback: The statement balance is the total owed.

Because reading lowers the APR
Because the minimum payment changes once you read it
To catch errors, unauthorized charges, and fees

questions.feedback: Checking each charge catches mistakes and fraud early.

sections.skill: Disputing a credit card billing error

questions.prompt: Ana sees a $59 charge on her card statement for an item she returned. Under the Fair Credit Billing Act, how long does she generally have to dispute it in writing?

choices.text: 60 days after the statement was sent
Within 2 business days after the purchase
1 year after the purchase
There is no time limit

questions.correct_answer: 60 days after the statement was sent
questions.intro: The Fair Credit Billing Act lets you dispute billing errors on credit card statements, such as charges for goods not received, returned items not credited, or wrong amounts. Send a written dispute within 60 days after the statement with the error was sent.
questions.feedback: Write to the issuer within 60 days after the statement with the error was sent.
sources: CFPB (Credit CARD Act / Regulation Z): Card issuers must mail statements at least 21 days before the due date; statements show the minimum payment warning; applicants under 21 need independent income or a cosigner. (https://www.consumerfinance.gov/consumer-tools/credit-cards/answers/key-terms/)

questions.prompt: While Ana's $59 billing dispute is investigated, what must she pay?

choices.text: Nothing at all on the whole account until it is settled
The disputed $59 first
A $59 dispute fee
The rest of the bill, but not the disputed $59

questions.correct_answer: The rest of the bill, but not the disputed $59
questions.intro: During a billing dispute, you can withhold payment of the disputed amount (and related charges) but must pay the undisputed part of the bill.
questions.feedback: She pays undisputed amounts; the disputed charge is on hold during the investigation.

questions.prompt: Where should Ana send a billing-error dispute?

choices.text: To the store's social media page
To the IRS
The issuer's billing-inquiries address
To the three credit bureaus, but not the issuer

questions.intro: Your statement lists where to send billing questions. A written dispute to that address protects your rights under the Fair Credit Billing Act.
questions.feedback: Written disputes go to the issuer's billing-inquiries address.
sources: CFPB (Credit CARD Act / Regulation Z): Card issuers must mail statements at least 21 days before the due date; statements show the minimum payment warning; applicants under 21 need independent income or a cosigner. questions.prompt: Which situation is a billing error Ana can dispute?

choices.text: She regrets buying a jacket she wore
She forgot she made a purchase but did make it
She was charged twice for one purchase
She wishes the APR were lower

questions.correct_answer: She was charged twice for one purchase
questions.feedback: Duplicate charges, wrong amounts, and items not delivered are billing errors.

misconceptions.A: Buyer's remorse is not an error

questions.prompt: A fraudulent $300 charge appears on Ana's credit card. Under federal law, what is the most she can be held responsible for?

choices.text: $0 in every case by law

questions.intro: For unauthorized credit card charges, federal law caps your liability at $50. Many issuers offer $0 liability as a policy.
questions.feedback: Federal law caps credit card liability for unauthorized charges at $50.

questions.prompt: A statement closes May 20, and payment is due June 15. Rosa makes a $200 purchase on May 22. On which statement will it first appear?

choices.text: The statement that closes June 20
The statement that closed May 20
It will never appear
A separate bill mailed the next day

questions.intro: The closing date ends a billing cycle. Purchases after the closing date appear on the next statement.
questions.feedback: Purchases after May 20 go on the next cycle's statement.

questions.prompt: How many days are there from a May 20 closing date to a June 15 due date?

choices.text: 26 days
21 days
15 days
31 days

questions.intro: The legal minimum time between mailing a statement and its due date is 21 days.
questions.feedback: 11 days left in May (21–31) + 15 days in June = 26 days.

questions.prompt: Rosa's payment is due June 15. Her bank says online payments take 1–2 business days to arrive. When should she pay to be safe?

choices.text: On June 16
Exactly at 11:59 p.m. on June 15, the last minute
Any time in June
A few business days before June 15

questions.correct_answer: A few business days before June 15
questions.intro: A payment counts when the issuer receives it. Paying a few days early avoids late fees from processing delays.
questions.feedback: Paying a few business days early makes sure it arrives on time.
sources: CFPB (Credit CARD Act / Regulation Z): Card issuers must mail statements at least 21 days before the due date; statements show the minimum payment warning; applicants under 21 need independent income or a cosigner. questions.prompt: Which autopay setting guarantees the account is never late and never charged purchase interest?

choices.text: Autopay for the minimum payment only, every month
Autopay for $10 a month
Autopay for the full statement balance
No autopay, paying when remembered

questions.correct_answer: Autopay for the full statement balance
questions.intro: Most card issuers let you set autopay for the minimum, a fixed amount, or the full statement balance.
questions.feedback: Paying the full statement balance automatically avoids late fees and purchase interest.

misconceptions.A: Avoids late fees but not interest

questions.prompt: If Rosa pays $300 toward a $412.75 statement balance, what happens to the grace period on new purchases?

choices.text: It stays the same, since she paid more than the minimum
It doubles
It applies only to purchases over $100
It is usually lost until she pays a full balance again

questions.correct_answer: It is usually lost until she pays a full balance again
questions.intro: The grace period on new purchases usually applies only when the previous statement balance was paid in full.
questions.feedback: Carrying any balance usually ends the grace period, so new purchases can start accruing interest.
